tasks.title: Persist custom themes in the preference store at version 6
tasks.description: Hard. Bump the preference store to version 6 with a custom_themes section beside project_library, change AppSettings::theme to ThemeSelection while keeping built-in selections serialized as the existing bare string, add Preferences::save_custom_themes, and make resolved_theme return a ResolvedTheme for built-in or custom selections with the follow-system rules unchanged. The custom section is user-authored data: malformed, duplicate or over-bound content refuses later writes instead of being dropped. Read docs/development/themes/spec.md section 'Store migration' and crates/app/docs/writes-and-persistence.md first; every caller of settings.theme (picker selection state, layout trace, apply_appearance) must compile against ThemeSelection.

acceptance.description: A test loads a complete version-5 store (settings with "theme":"nord", recents, drafts, project names, project library) and asserts every section is identical, custom_themes is empty, and loading did not rewrite the file.

Saving writes "version": 6; a store with two custom themes and "theme": {"custom": 2} loads, resolves to that palette, and round-trips byte-for-byte through save; the existing saved_daylight_remains_braden test still sees "daylight" as a bare string.

Duplicate ids, duplicate names (case-insensitive), a 33rd theme, an invalid hex token or an invalid name make load_from fail so a later save_settings refuses and leaves the original bytes intact; a {"custom": 99} selection with no such theme resolves to the default theme without a write.

save_custom_themes rereads the disk store before merging (a test changes settings on disk between load and save and both survive), runs on the preference executor, and resolved_theme keeps the existing follow-system behavior for built-ins and applies the spec's rule to light and dark custom themes under both appearances, with tests.
crates/app/docs/writes-and-persistence.md documents the custom-theme section, its bounds, the refusal policy and the version-6 migration, and `python3 scripts/gate.py fast` is green.

tasks.title: Cut the Settings and theme editor frame cost to meet the live-preview budget
tasks.description: Hard. An early measurement of the theme editor (candidate bb9f332 of an earlier run) recorded ten consecutive live-preview edits at median 45 ms and p95 56.6 ms against the 16 ms budget in docs/development/themes/spec.md section 'Performance', on the themes-apply-trace fixture at scale 2 on the Linux baseline host. apply_appearance costs under 0.2 ms; the time is a whole-window layout, paint and present of Settings plus the editor dialog (about 20 ms at 2x), paid twice when a keystroke renders in the old palette before the coalesced apply, and a Settings switch also draws a second frame when the preference save completes (settings.rs save_preferences notifies unconditionally). Reduce the frame cost in the application path, as the spec's open question on full-window repaints directs: render once per edit and once per switch, avoid re-laying-out or re-painting what a palette change does not alter, and cheapen the twenty theme preview cards and the dialog's rows. Do not change the budget, the gitturtle.theme_apply_frame_ms boundaries recorded in docs/benchmarks/metrics.md, or the visible design.

acceptance.description: In release mode on the themes-apply-trace fixture at 2x scale, ten consecutive editor live-preview edits measured with the unchanged gitturtle.theme_apply_frame_ms edit trace have p95 ≤ 16 ms; docs/benchmarks/ gains a dated record with build identity, host, cache state, raw samples and a before/after comparison against the themes-editor record, and the performance-reviewer attests it.

The same record shows 60 Settings theme switches cycling ThemeChoice::ALL on that fixture with median ≤ 8 ms and p95 ≤ 16 ms, and UI-thread CPU per switch, measured as in docs/benchmarks/2026-09-18-theme-apply.md, no higher than that baseline's.

A #[gpui::test] shows that a burst of editor edits and a Settings theme switch each lead to exactly one window draw after the handler: no draw in the old palette before the draft is applied and no second draw from a preference-save completion that changes nothing visible.

native-qa re-runs the committed docs/evidence/themes/editor/ captures and the Settings picker captures against the new build and reports no differing pixels outside measured-timing text, or the design-reviewer approves each difference against DESIGN.md.

tasks.commit: perf(settings): cut the Settings and theme editor frame cost
